text: When this passion is exorbitant, it is dangerous in all men, and in those who govern a commonwealth, utterly destructive. For in the possession of large power and authority, it transports men to a degree of madness; so that now they no more think what is good, glorious, but will have those actions only esteemed good that are glorious.
author: Plutarch
translation: John Dryden et al., rev. Arthur Hugh Clough, 1864
